title: PsiQuantum Debuts 8x8 Optical Circuit Switch for AI Infrastructure
summary:
The quantum computing firm has demoed a new photonics-based networking device intended to address hardware bottlenecks in data centers caused by the expansion of artificial intelligence. The 8x8 Optical Circuit Switch (OCS) uses a silicon photonics platform that PsiQuantum spent nearly 10 years developing for its quantum hardware.

The device has an insertion loss of about 1.2 dB, which the company says is comparable to MEMS switches and more efficient than competitors such as Salience and iPronics. However, the OCS reconfigures in under 3 ms, which is slower than the reconfiguration times of iPronics (under 1 ms) and Salience's 64x64 switch (under 300 µs), limiting its use to scale-out connections rather than in-rack switching.

AI is pushing computing infrastructure to its limits. Our photonics can help.

Today, PsiQuantum is unveiling its industry-leading Optical Circuit Switch initiative with an 8×8 OCS demo built on the company’s low-loss silicon photonics platform—the same platform we’ve spent nearly a decade developing for quantum computing.

selectedTweets.text: PsiQuantum say their OCS has around 1.2 dB of inesrtion loss and needs no amplifier, so putting it on par with a MEMS switch. Salience’s and iPronics’ SiPh switches lose several dB on the chip alone, so they are still well behind on IL. PsiQuantum trails on speed, however, and the obvious radix. They claim that their switch takes under 3 ms to reconfigure compared with under 300 µs for Salience’s full 64 × 64 switch and under 1 ms quoted by iPronics. PsiQuantum’s demo is also only 8x8 so it might not remain rosy as they scale radix. The low insertion loss makes their OCS competitive with free-space switches for scale-out connections and reconfiguration between training runs, but at around 3 ms, it remains too slow for the in-rack switching applications, which is what Salience and iPronics are targeting.
